About 24,000 Jews lived in Palestine in 1882 (about 0.3% of world Jewry); Ottoman records of 1878 list 15,011 Jews among 462,465 residents. Arabic-speaking Musta'arabim Jews had lived there since before the coming of Islam; Sephardic communities came in the late Mamluk and early Ottoman periods, Ashkenazi immigrants in the 18th and 19th centuries.

Genetic studies find Ashkenazi Jews to be a mixture of Middle Eastern (most likely Levantine) and European ancestry, with estimates of the Middle Eastern share ranging from about a fifth to over half depending on method; Ashkenazi, Sephardi and Mizrahi Jews are closer to one another than to their host populations, and among the closest genetic neighbours of most Jewish groups are Palestinians, Bedouin, Druze and Southern Europeans.
The Rio Treaty was signed on 2 September 1947 in Rio de Janeiro.
The Convention for European Economic Cooperation was signed in Paris on 16 April 1948.
Golda Meyerson (Meir) raised about $50 million in the United States for the Haganah in early 1948.
